properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 31 at 11:03AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations 8 to 14
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...From 5 PM Sunday to 11 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, especially Sunday night
and Monday morning. Strong winds could produce areas of blowing and
drifting snow.
properties.areaDesc: Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 31 at 10:37AM MDT until November 2 at 12:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 10, 000 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 12 and 18 inches, with locally higher amounts
possible. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Northwest San Juan Mountains and Southwest San Juan
Mountains.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Sunday to noon MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.
properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 31 at 10:37AM MDT until November 2 at 6:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected above 10, 000 feet. Total snow accumulations
between 5 and 10 inches. Locally higher amounts possible. Winds
gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Flat Tops, Gore and Elk Mountains/Central Mountain Valleys,
Grand and Battlement Mesas, and West Elk and Sawatch Mountains.

* WHEN...From noon Sunday to 6 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning and evening commutes.
properties.areaDesc: Grand and Battlement Mesas; Gore and Elk Mountains/Central Mountain Valleys; West Elk and Sawatch Mountains; Flat Tops

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 9:50AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

La Plata River at Hesperus affecting La Plata County.

For the La Plata River...including Hesperus...Minor flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 900 AM MST.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...La Plata River at Hesperus.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM MDT Saturday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Sunday
evening to a crest of 5.8 feet late Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.8
feet on 05/21/2005.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 9:42AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...Major flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 845 AM MST.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday evening.

- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.

feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 5:48AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
properties.areaDesc: Upper Rio Grande Valley/Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Ft; Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 5:48AM MDT until November 4 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be possible,
especially over the western half of San Luis Valley.

* WHERE...The western half of the San Luis Valley, including Del
Norte, Antonito and Mogote.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Runoff from heavy rain and melting snow over the San Juan
Mountains may cause flooding in the San Luis Valley, especially
Monday and Tuesday as high flows move out of the mountains and
through the Rio Grande and Conejos River.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Del Norte Vicinity/Northern San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Alamosa  Vicinity/Central San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Southern San Luis Valley

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 30 at 3:02PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges
